findings.reason: without the receipt required on the settled path, the section certifies an outcome whose only guard (the archive receipt and its disposable-graph refusal) applies to a route the settle clause explicitly does not require.
findings.text: the clause "a name of the pair that `sn-definitions-by-construction` §6 has already brought onto the ruled spelling is recorded as settled with the edit that settled it" accepts "the edit that settled it" as sufficient, while every other route in this section onto that spelling is required to be "the history-apart reclaim ... with its archive receipt"; because the ruled spelling is a live `status: superseded` tombstone holding reviews and lineage, a §6 settle that lands on it by any other write would be recorded as settled while that history is lost, and the "no other tombstone is revived" clause cannot catch it since this is that same tombstone

response_events.note: A name of the pair counts as settled by the live rewrite only where that edit was the history-apart reclaim with its archive receipt; otherwise it is reported to the lead as a revived tombstone.

done_when-1.note: A name of the pair counts as settled by the live rewrite only where that edit was the history-apart reclaim with its archive receipt; otherwise it is reported to the lead as a revived tombstone.
